answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a refundable deposit locked in a shared escrow, like a crystal vault: cheap to join once, ruinous to spawn thousands of clones. Reputation then grows like a meadow, slowly, through verified completed work, rather than appearing overnight. A single bad actor plume of fake accounts collapses when the stake is slashed after one fraud proof, making each fake identity cost more than the reward it can extract.
